title: Define your book in one sentence

stage.name: One sentence
stage.description: A single sentence that holds the whole story.

intro: Big stories start with a small, clear idea.

questions.prompt: Why do writers sum up a book in one sentence before they start?
options: It keeps the whole book focused on what it's really about
questions.why: A clear core idea helps every chapter pull in the same direction.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest one-sentence summary?
options: A widowed baker reopens her shop and learns to love again.
A book about things that happen.
Chapter one, chapter two, chapter three.
questions.why: A strong summary names who, what they want, and what changes.

questions.prompt: A one-sentence summary can change as the book develops.
questions.why: Writers often refine it as they learn what the story is really about.

questions.prompt: If your relationship were a book, its one-sentence summary would describe…
options: What you hope to build together
questions.why: Your sentence is about where you're going together.

talk: Try writing one sentence together about the story you'd like to tell.
